prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance/transfer→screening/sortation/make-up→Outbound Load Control Desk; excludes airline loading. States: operational hold/safe stop; no explicit modes. Elements/flows: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit stages flight-associated bags. Bag Tag Printer produces tags/Calibration Witness Tag; replacement requires authorized identity-confirmation. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) supplies operating-departure/flight/destination/date/timing; Flight Cutoff Advisory→Baggage Control System (Velvet): alarms/routes; authoritative identity/flight/screening-disposition/handling-status. Transfer Bag Feeder meters transfers; Late Transfer Bag Card→Bag Reconciliation Station: flight-match/location/identity verification, Bag Match Query. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) assigns authorized screening-preserving lanes/routes; Recovery Route Card→Maintenance Technician consultation before return-to-service. Induction Tray Conveyor safely meters readable-identity/valid-route bags. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel) records tag/image; South Gate Scanner verifies identity, Manual Rescan Receipt→Image Resolution Desk: approved-recapture verification; Oversize Exception Ticket→desk: authorized-position confirmation. Desk assesses images/records disposition before continuation. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) routes cleared bags to assigned make-up destinations/diverts unresolved; Chute Occupancy Note→Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern): capacity verification. Secondary Inspection Chute controls examination/retention; excludes unrelated bags. East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor deliver controlled flows. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) preserves positions/order; Carousel Release Slip←Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms flight/position/staffing/equipment/sequence; release requires valid screening-disposition/destination. Outbound Load Control Desk verifies eligibility/reconciliation. Explosives Response Team (Pebble) secures/assesses events/directs handling/communicates disposition through approved channels; produces Custody Seal Log→Security Duty Manager: seal-accountability/discrepancy-escalation; manager resolves holds/response-access. Tern coordinates actors/airport security personnel/airline ground operations, approves exceptions, communicates holds/stops unsafe induction; assigns hold/route-exception owners before continuation. Requirements: monitored custody screening-release→authorized-loading-handoff; task-authorized access; preserve bag-flight association; uncertain identity/unresolved screening→inspection/controlled-hold/escalation. Both scanners healthy before release-reliance; faults hold feed. Velvet authorizes checked reentry; route/flight changes require

New part:
S218: The Bag Reconciliation Station compares scanned bag identities against the expected flight population and flags missing or duplicate records for resolution.
S219: The Airline Ramp Coordinator uses the Bag Match Query to review unresolved bag-to-flight mismatches before loading authorization is granted.
S220: The East Make-Up Conveyor moves reconciled bags toward the correct flight position without bypassing required identity checks.
S221: The West Make-Up Conveyor remains subject to the same controlled access and reconciliation rules as other make-up equipment.
S222: The Transfer Bag Feeder accepts transfer bags only when their identity and intended onward flight can be verified.
S223: The Outbound Load Control Desk confirms that the flight assignment, reconciled bag count, and operational status are consistent before accepting the loading record.
S224: Before aircraft loading, the Airline Ramp Coordinator verifies that the bag identity is readable, the flight assignment is current, and the security disposition permits loading.
S225: The physical bags presented for loading must agree with the reconciled records, and every unexplained count or identity difference blocks acceptance.
S226: A bag is ready for departure only after screening release, custody continuity, final reconciliation, and loading checks are all complete and recorded.
S227: Operational monitoring provides a continuous view of baggage throughput, equipment availability, queue growth, screening status, and reconciliation exceptions.
S228: The Baggage Control System records bag events and reports missing, duplicate, or delayed event sequences for operational review.
S229: The Concourse Zone Controller reports equipment state changes and alarm conditions to the operations monitoring function.
S230: The Induction Tray Conveyor is monitored for stops, accumulation, and sustained operation below its approved rate.
S231: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter is monitored for availability, recirculation, fault frequency, and output rate against the approved operating plan.
S232: North Gate Scanner performance is assessed using availability, image capture quality, alarm frequency, and screening completion records.
S233: South Gate Scanner performance is assessed using the same approved service measures and screening completion criteria.
S234: The Image Resolution Desk reports unresolved images, review backlog, and processing time against the locally approved service target.
S235: The Bag Reconciliation Station reports unmatched records and count differences, which remain subject to resolution before acceptance.
S236: The Flight Data Gateway is monitored for message timeliness, completeness, and interface errors affecting flight assignment data.
S237: The Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit is monitored for service availability, transaction completion, and accumulation at its entry point.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
